To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
p-c-Jun is a pivotal factor in colorectal tumorigenesis and that it is important to determine its expression in colorectal cancer patients.
p-c-Jun is expressed in colorectal tumors and that its expression is correlated with that of TCF4 and the transcriptional target of TCF, MMP7.
p-c-Jun expression is significantly increased in colorectal tumors and that p-cJun expression in adenomas and intraepithelial lesions is negatively correlated with tumor progression.

the expression of p-c-JUN, TCF4, and β-catenin in colorectum cancer.
the expression of p-cJun, TCF4, beta-catenin and MMP-7 in colorectal cancer.

nuclear expression of TCF4 and p-c-Jun may be a useful prognostic marker of human colorectal tumor progression.

nuclear expression of the three proteins, p-c-Jun, β-catenin, and TCF4, are important in human colorectal tumorigenesis, and that the p-c-Jun may be a key factor in the earlier stages.

p-c-Jun, which has been reported to be a key transcription factor in the Wnt pathway in mice, is a critical factor in the early stages of colorectal carcinogenesis in humans.
